exposure: Pelvimetry using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) prior to attempted vaginal breech delivery
cohort: The study involved 160 primigravidas with breech presentation who attempted vaginal breech delivery, compared with four external study cohorts that used MRI as a selection criterion.
finding: The study concluded that pelvimetry has not been shown to predict neonatal outcome and that delivery outcomes are more dependent on the competence of the obstetric delivering team rather than pelvimetry.
mod_finding: The vaginal delivery rate in the cohort without MRI (65.6%) was comparable to rates in studies using prior MRI as a selection criterion (65.4% to 67.5%).
